newsitem.title: USA: Two Georgia lawmakers retaliate against New York.
newsitem.headline: Two Georgia lawmakers retaliate against New York.

text.p: Two Georgia lawmakers who thought New York Gov. George Pataki insulted their state flag took revenge Tuesday on the Empire State flag.
Republican State Sens. Eric Johnson and Joey Brush took a screwdriver to the fourth-floor gallery of the gold-domed capitol and removed the New York flag from its place of honour.

"We didn't start it, they did," Brush told Reuters. "To us, this is not an issue of the Georgia flag. The issue to me is that New York has no business, no say in this. This flag belongs to the people of the state of Georgia. And until they change it, it's the official flag."
Monday Pataki denounced the Georgia state flag as a "symbol of hatred" and removed it from the New York capitol building in Albany.

The Georgia flag, which includes the crossed bars of the Confederate battle symbol, had hung in the New York capitol for about 20 years. Its removal was prompted by complaints from a group of black legislators.

The Confederate emblem is considered offensive by many black Americans. Civil rights leaders in Georgia have unsuccessfully sought its removal for years. Gov. Zell Miller failed to have the Confederate symbol removed in 1993.

"Some of us Georgians are offended by Gen. Sherman. But we're not asking that he be erased from history," said Brush, referring to the Union general whose soldiers burned Atlanta to the ground during the Civil War.
According to eyewitnesses, Johnson and Brush leaped over a railing about 60 feet above the capitol floor Tuesday and unscrewed the hinges to the New York flag.

The pair then pulled the banner from its perch, paraded it through the capitol to the cheers of onlookers. They took it to the office of Secretary of State Lewis Massey and asked it be kept out of sight until New York returned the Georgia flag to its rightful place.

Massey issued a statement accusing officials in both states of "childish" antics and said, "We will return New York's flag to its proper place ... and we will do so in a dignified manner that does not invite publicity."
Meanwhile Republican members of the Georgia House of Representatives introduced a resolution condemning New York's action and sanctioning retaliatory measures.

But State Representative Tyrone Brooks, leader of the Georgia Association of Black Elected Officials, said he hoped other states would follow New York's lead. "I'm sending a letter to Gov. Pataki commending him for his bold action against racism," he said.
